subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Shelf Placement Science
description: A micro-lesson that makes Shelf Placement Science usable.

hook.text: Products at eye level sell 35% more than those on the bottom shelf. Same product, same price, different height.

buildup.text: Retailers charge brands for premium shelf space. Eye-level placement is prime real estate.

discovery.text: Children's cereals are placed at children's eye level. The character on the box looks downward, making eye contact.

twist.text: Store brands are on the bottom shelf not because they are worse but because premium brands paid to push them down.

climax.text: Look up and down, not just straight ahead. The best value is often on shelves you are engineered to ignore.

punchline.text: What you see first is what someone paid to put there.

quiz.question: Why are children's cereals placed lower on shelves?
options: They are lighter and easier to stock low
They are positioned at children's eye level to attract their attention
Store policy groups all cereals by brand alphabetically
